chunks: And whatever is in this book, narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood, I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood. And I have transmitted it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad Al-Maliki, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood. And I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah; and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood.

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي مَهْمُودٍ: Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood, a key narrator
key_terms.الصَّفَّارِ: Al-Saffar, a nisba indicating profession or origin
key_terms.الْمَالِكِيِّ: Al-Maliki, a nisba indicating origin or affiliation
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific for companions/scholars

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood's narrations verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs the technique of *takhrij* (verification) by presenting multiple independent chains (*tawatur* in a loose sense) to authenticate the reliability of Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood, a key narrator in the Kufan school. By citing his own father, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ibrahim, and other prominent figures like al-Majilawayh and al-Saffar, he underscores the robustness and widespread acceptance of these narrations within the Shia scholarly tradition.
